commands.review_summary:
The branch removes sole-tab fallback adoption, snapshots pre-action target IDs for `/act`, chooses a unique newly observed or navigated-URL target as a replacement, adds regression tests, and includes a Chrome/CDP proof harness.

PR surface: Source +241, Tests +22. Total +263 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-level reproduction is concrete: the supplied current bug report and PR test describe a selected tab disappearing while an unrelated tab survives. A direct current-main execution was not available in this read-only review environment.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A maintainer must choose the permanent browser target-identity contract before an automated repair can safely reshape this branch.

target.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a browser navigation or action invalidates the selected raw target, `resolveTargetIdAfterNavigate` retried once and then adopted **any** sole remaining tab, regardless of whether that tab matched the acted-on page:

```ts
if (options?.allowSingleTabFallback && tabs.length === 1) {
  return { targetId: tabs[0]?.targetId ?? opts.oldTargetId, shouldRetry: false };
}
```

The shared resolver backs both `/navigate` and `/act`. So if an action closed or replaced the selected target while an unrelated tab stayed open at a different URL, `/act` could return that unrelated tab's `targetId`. A caller that trusts the response then continues its next mutating action on the wrong page. The focused test even asserted this: old target `old-123`, sole unrelated tab `only-tab` at a different URL, expected result `only-tab`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sole-tab adoption, tab ordering, and a bare URL match are not proof of identity. The response target must be the backend-owned identity of the page that actually executed the operation. When that identity is gone and continuity cannot be proven, the resolver should return the acted-on (now stale or closed) identity so the caller requires a fresh selection, rather than guessing a tab.

The codebase already draws this distinction elsewhere: the post-interaction navigation guard separates newly-appeared tabs from pre-existing ones by their initial target ids, and default tab selection returns `null` ("require a fresh explicit choice") when a sticky target disappears without a proven migration. This change brings the post-action resolver up to the same standard.

## User Impact

A replacement is now adopted only when continuity is provable:

- **Provable replacement (with a pre-action snapshot):** the acted-on page was replaced by a target that did **not** exist before the operation. Exactly one such newly-appeared target is adopted. A pre-existing unrelated tab is never adopted, which fixes the reported wrong-tab routing.
- **Provable renderer swap (navigate path):** exactly one candidate now sits at the URL we just navigated to (Chrome detaches the old renderer target and reattaches the same tab under a new raw target). URL equality is trusted only against the just-navigated URL, never a stale pre-action URL, tab ordering, or a sole remaining tab.
- **Unproven:** the backend-owned acted-on identity is returned so the caller re-selects.

The `/act` route now snapshots tab ids just before the Playwright action and passes them to the resolver. Prior continuity is preserved: `chrome-extension://` to HTTPS navigation (#25323 / #25326) and action-triggered target replacement (#46137) still resolve to the correct replacement.

## Evidence

### Live browser proof (real Chrome over CDP)

A standalone harness (`extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.mts`) launches a real Chrome instance and reads its live targets through `Target.getTargets`, the same CDP surface the plugin's `listTabs` uses. The genuine raw target ids and URLs are fed into the shipped `resolveTargetIdAfterNavigate`. Nothing is mocked; URLs are redacted in the transcript.

Run:

```
pnpm exec tsx extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.mts
```

Redacted output:

```
=== Live-browser proof for #103785 (real Chrome over CDP) ===

Scenario A: action closes acted-on tab A; unrelated tab B survives

  pre-action targets (real CDP):
    - target=48DEEFC6… url=data:<UNRELATED-B>
    - target=19F1C22F… url=data:<ACTED-ON-A>
  post-action targets (real CDP):
    - target=48DEEFC6… url=data:<UNRELATED-B>

  resolver returned target=19F1C22F… (A=19F1C22F…, B=48DEEFC6…)
  kept acted-on identity A: true
  adopted unrelated survivor B: false
  PASS: unrelated survivor B was NOT adopted.

Scenario B: renderer swap (old raw target detached, page reattaches at navigated url)

  pre-navigate targets (real CDP):
    - target=7AC30457… url=data:<PRE-SWAP>
  post-navigate targets (real CDP):
    - target=F4202B71… url=data:<SWAPPED>

  resolver returned target=F4202B71… (old=7AC30457…, reattached=F4202B71…)
  adopted reattached target at navigated url: true
  PASS: renderer-swap continuity preserved.

=== ALL SCENARIOS PASSED ===
```

- **Scenario A (the reported bug):** tab A is acted on and closed while an unrelated tab B stays open. After the action only B remains, yet the resolver returns A's backend-owned identity and never adopts B. Before this change the sole-tab fallback would have returned B and routed the next action onto the wrong page.
- **Scenario B (continuity preserved):** the acted-on raw target is detached and the page reattaches under a new raw target at the just-navigated URL. The resolver adopts the reattached target, so renderer-swap / action-triggered replacement paths keep working.

### Source and test changes

- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot-target.ts`: removed the sole-tab fallback; adopt only a uniquely newly-appeared target, or the single candidate at the just-navigated URL.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts`: capture pre-action target ids (reusing the existing-session `initialTabTargetIds`, and a new snapshot for the Playwright path) and pass them as `knownTargetIds`.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts`: the "sole unrelated tab" case now asserts the acted-on identity is kept; added a regression test for a sole tab matching only a stale URL.

Automated tests (focused + full browser extension suite):

```
pnpm test:extension browser -- extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts
# Test Files 2 passed (2) | Tests 34 passed (34)

pnpm test:extension browser
# Tests 1887 passed | 1 skipped
# (the only failure, doctor-browser "skips Chrome auto-detection", also fails on a clean checkout: it depends on a local Chrome install)
```

Extension package boundary typecheck: `extension package boundary check passed`.

Closes #103785
